articles.title: Vídeo: veja o que Fernando Sastre confessou para reduzir pena em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Condenação de Fernando Sastre foi fixada em 17 anos, 1 mês e 10 dias de prisão após juíza reconhecer como atenuante a confissão parcial feita no júri. Defesa defendia homicídio culposo, com pena de 2 a 4 anos, enquanto o MP recorrerá para punição superior a 20 anos.
articles.summary: Condenação de Fernando Sastre foi fixada em 17 anos, 1 mês e 10 dias de prisão após juíza reconhecer como atenuante a confissão parcial feita no júri.
articles.body:
A confissão feita pelo empresário Fernando Sastre Filho durante o julgamento na semana passada no Fórum Criminal da Barra Funda, na Zona Oeste de São Paulo, teve efeito direto na pena de pouco mais de 17 anos de prisão aplicada pela Justiça contra ele pela morte do motorista de aplicativo Ornaldo da Silva Viana. O interrogatório foi gravado (veja vídeo acima) .

Ao admitir pela primeira vez que havia consumido bebida alcoólica antes de dirigir o Porsche que atingiu o carro da vítima em 31 de março de 2024, Sastre obteve uma redução de cerca de um ano e meio na condenação que receberia, que seria de mais de 18 anos.

Ornaldo, de 52 anos, dirigia um Renault Sandero quando foi atingido pelo Porsche conduzido pelo empresário. A batida foi gravada por câmeras de monitoramento (veja abaixo) .

Fernando Sastre Filho durante seu interrogatório no Fórum Criminal da Barra Funda, Zona Oeste de São Paulo. — Foto: Reprodução

A admissão de que havia ingerido álcool antes de dirigir levou a juíza Melanie Liesenberg a reconhecer parcialmente a atenuante da confissão espontânea após a decisão majoritária dos jurados pela condenação. Sem o benefício, a pena seria de aproximadamente 18 anos, 6 meses e 28 dias de prisão.

Com a redução de 1/12, a condenação foi fixada em 17 anos, 1 mês e 10 dias pelos crimes de homicídio qualificado por perigo comum, na modalidade de dolo eventual, pela morte de Ornaldo, e lesão corporal gravíssima contra Marcus Vinicius Machado Rocha, amigo de Sastre que ocupava o banco do passageiro do Porsche no momento da colisão.

No interrogatório realizado na quinta-feira (30), segundo e último dia do júri, Sastre abandonou a versão que sustentava desde o acidente que provocou em 31 de março de 2024, de que havia bebido apenas água. E reconheceu que havia consumido bebida alcoólica antes de assumir a direção do carro.

Vídeos do julgamento obtidos pela equipe de reportagem mostram o empresário emocionado durante o interrogatório, que durou cerca de uma hora e dez minutos.

No início da fala aos jurados, ele afirmou: "Eu poderia inventar mil desculpas, mas estou aqui entregue a esse plenário, eu acredito na Justiça. Hoje quero dizer a verdade."

Em seguida, fez a admissão que manteve em segredo desde o acidente: "Confesso, sim, que, no dia dos fatos, eu ingeri bebida alcoólica."

O empresário Fernando Sastre, que matou o motorista de aplicativo Ornaldo da Silva Viana. — Foto: Reprodução

Ao detalhar o que consumiu antes de assumir a direção do Porsche, declarou: "Eu bebi dois drinks."

Questionado sobre por que havia escondido essa informação durante a investigação e o processo, respondeu: "Não tem justificativa para isso que eu fiz. Eu me arrependo profundamente de não ter contado a verdade desde o início."

Em outro momento, afirmou: "Eu me desculpo a todos aqueles que eu ofendi por não ter dito a verdade. E que hoje eu quero sim dizer a verdade."

Fernando Sastre Filho confessou ter bebido e dirigido. — Foto: Reprodução

Sastre também pediu desculpas à família do motorista de aplicativo: "Eu imagino toda dor e sofrimento que eles estão sentindo. O seu Ornaldo tinha quase a mesma idade do meu pai. Posso imaginar o que eles estão sentindo e toda a devastação."

A juíza considerou que essas declarações justificaram a aplicação da atenuante da confissão, mas ressaltou que ela foi apenas parcial porque Sastre admitiu ter consumido álcool e provocado a colisão, mas continuou negando ter assumido o risco de matar.

A confissão do consumo de álcool marcou uma mudança importante na estratégia da defesa de Sastre. Durante toda a investigação, em depoimentos à polícia e até em entrevista ao Fantástico , em maio de 2024, o empresário sustentava que não havia ingerido bebida alcoólica e que havia consumido apenas água (veja vídeo acima) .

A nova versão apresentada aos jurados se aproximou de relatos colhidos desde o início das investigações. Marcus, sobrevivente da batida, reafirmou no julgamento que o então amigo havia consumido bebida alcoólica antes de dirigir . A namorada de Marcus à época, Juliana de Toledo Simões, também prestou depoimento no mesmo sentido.

Marcus sofreu ferimentos graves no acidente. Ele perdeu o baço, fraturou cinco costelas e ficou cerca de dez dias internado, parte desse período na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) de um hospital.

O processo reúne ainda um vídeo gravado por amigos pouco antes da batida. Nas imagens, Fernando aparece conversando com fala considerada pastosa, característica associada à embriaguez (assista acima) . No mesmo registro, sua então namorada é ouvida pedindo para que ele não dirigisse o Porsche.

Testemunhas que chegaram ao local logo após a colisão e prestaram depoimento à polícia e ao Tribunal do Júri também relataram que o empresário apresentava sinais de embriaguez. Algumas disseram que ele cambaleava após sair do veículo.

Imagens de câmeras corporais registraram bombeiros comentando, ainda no local da ocorrência, que o empresário aparentava estar alcoolizado (veja vídeo acima) . Mesmo assim, ele foi liberado por policiais militares e não passou pelo teste do bafômetro para confirmar se havia bebido e dirigido.

Promotores Rodolfo Morais e Lucas Schaefer. — Foto: Kleber Tomaz/g1

Após a sentença, os promotores Rodolfo Morais e Lucas Schaefer informaram à equipe de reportagem que vão recorrer na Justiça para tentar elevar a condenação para mais de 20 anos de prisão . Segundo eles, a punição ficou abaixo do que o Ministério Público considera compatível com a gravidade do caso.

A batida aconteceu na madrugada de 31 de março de 2024, na Avenida Salim Farah Maluf, no Tatuapé, na Zona Leste de São Paulo. Segundo a acusação, Sastre dirigia embriagado e em alta velocidade quando atingiu a traseira do Renault Sandero conduzido por Ornaldo.

Laudo do Instituto de Criminalística concluiu que o Porsche atingiu 156 km/h antes da colisão e ainda estava a cerca de 136 km/h no momento do impacto , em uma via cujo limite era de 50 km/h.

A promotora Monique Ratton foi responsável por pedir a prisão preventiva de Sastre durante a fase de investigação, medida posteriormente acolhida pela Justiça.

Preso preventivamente desde 6 de maio de 2024, Sastre já cumpriu cerca de dois anos e cinco meses de prisão, período que será abatido da condenação. Mantida a sentença e desconsiderados eventuais benefícios previstos na legislação, restariam aproximadamente 14 anos e 8 meses de pena, com término estimado, em tese, por volta de 2041.

Sastre tem atualmente 27 anos. Se a condenação for mantida e cumprida integralmente, ele deixaria a prisão por volta dos 41 anos de idade. Atualmente cumpre a pena em Potim, interior paulista .

Giovanna, namorada de Sastre (no detalhe), é expulsa do plenário do júri por juíza por mau comportamento. — Foto: Reprodução

O julgamento também foi marcado por episódios envolvendo a então namorada de Sastre, Giovana Pinheiro Silva.

Segundo o Ministério Público, Giovana foi expulsa do plenário pela juíza após fazer comentários e expressões de deboche durante depoimentos de testemunhas de acusação. A magistrada aplicou multa equivalente a 10 salários mínimos, cerca de R$ 16,4 mil.

O Ministério Público informou ainda que pretende responsabilizá-la por falso testemunho e solicitará a abertura de investigação pela Polícia Civil para apurar eventual prática de fraude processual.

Para os promotores, ela ajudou a sustentar durante a investigação e o processo a versão de que Sastre não havia consumido bebida alcoólica antes do acidente, informação posteriormente desmentida pelo próprio empresário em seu interrogatório.

Traseira do Renault Sandero branco ficou destruída após ser atingida pelo Porsche azul — Foto: Rômulo D'Ávila/TV Globo

A defesa de Sastre e de Giovana informou que recorrerá da condenação e que não concordou com a aplicação da multa.

Em nota, o advogado Jonas Marzagão afirmou:

"A defesa de Fernando Sastre informa que recebeu a decisão do Tribunal do Júri com serenidade, mas discorda frontalmente dos fundamentos e do resultado do julgamento. Reafirmamos nosso respeito à instituição do Júri, porém ressaltamos que a decisão contraria as provas dos autos. Informamos que interporemos o recurso cabível para reverter o julgamento perante o Tribunal de Justiça."

Além de Marzagão, atuam na defesa os advogados Eliseu Soares Neto, João Victor Gonçalves e Eugênio Malavasi.

Durante o julgamento, a defesa sustentou que o caso deveria ser desclassificado para homicídio culposo na direção de veículo automotor, hipótese em que não há intenção nem assunção do risco de matar. Se essa tese tivesse sido acolhida, a pena poderia variar de 2 a 4 anos de prisão.

articles.title: Veja prints: alunos de Medicina no Paraná enviaram mensagens com referência ao nazismo para atacar estudantes bolsistas após eleição | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministério Público Federal disse apurar o caso, registrado em universidade particular de Maringá. Mensagens foram enviadas após resultado do 2º turno das eleições. UniCesumar afirmou que alunos envolvidos foram expulsos, suspensos ou advertidos.
articles.summary: Ministério Público Federal disse apurar o caso, registrado em universidade particular de Maringá. Mensagens foram enviadas após resultado do 2º turno das eleições. UniCesumar afirmou que alunos envolvidos foram expulsos, suspensos ou advertidos.
articles.body:
Mensagens foram enviadas em um grupo com estudantes de medicina — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Alunos do curso de Medicina, que realizaram ataques a bolsistas e referências ao nazismo em um grupo de mensagens , foram expulsos de uma faculdade particular de Maringá , no Norte do Paraná. As mensagens foram enviadas depois do resultado das Eleições de 2026 , em que Lula foi reeleito presidente do Brasil .

A UniCesumar, instituição em que os alunos estudam, disse no sábado (31) que adotou medidas disciplinares para punir os alunos envolvidos . Além das expulsões, houve suspensões e advertências, "de acordo com a gravidade das condutas". O g1 questionou quantos estudantes receberam cada uma das punições, mas a universidade respondeu que não vai informar.

O g1 optou por não identificar os alunos, uma vez que o caso ainda está sendo investigado pelos órgãos responsáveis e pode envolver menores de idade.

As mensagens foram enviadas no domingo (25) em um grupo da turma. Em uma delas, um estudante sugere superioridade em relação aos bolsistas ao comparar quem paga a mensalidade com quem conquistou a vaga por seleção acadêmica de programas sociais.

"Quem paga trabalhou e tem 15 mil [reais] por mês para pagar >>>>>>> Quem passou numa provinha", escreveu um outro estudante.

Mensagens foram enviadas em um grupo com estudantes de medicina — Foto: Arquivo

Além disso, imagens e expressões associadas ao nazismo também foram compartilhadas nos grupos. Em uma das mensagens, um estudante compartilhou a foto do exército nazista acompanhada de referências ao "leite cru", expressão que se tornou comum entre grupos na internet que defendem a supremacia branca .

Print da conversa de cunho nazista. — Foto: Reprodução

Alunos da instituição abriram uma denúncia no Ministério Público Federal (MPF) depois dos ataques. O órgão confirmou ter recebido a denúncia sobre as mensagens e disse que apura o caso.

Ao g1 , um estudante informou que tanto os universitários que fizeram as ofensas quanto aqueles que foram alvos das mensagens não frequentaram a instituição desde que o caso ganhou repercussão.

"É um clima hostil na faculdade, um clima hostil nos grupos, que vai muito além de divergências políticas. Parece que o contexto da eleição foi apenas um pretexto para eles extravasarem o ódio às pessoas mais pobres", disse o estudante, que preferiu não ser identificado.

Em nota, a UniCesumar afirmou que adotou medidas disciplinares contra os alunos envolvidos nas mensagens, mas não detalhou quantos estudantes foram atingidos pela decisão. Veja a íntegra:

"A UniCesumar comunica que concluiu no dia 30 de outubro a Sindicância Interna aberta para apuração dos fatos envolvendo mensagens trocadas em grupo de WhatsApp por alunos da Instituição.

A Comissão de Sindicância recomendou e a Reitoria da Unicesumar decidiu pela aplicação de medidas disciplinares em relação aos alunos envolvidos, nos termos do Regimento Interno da universidade.

As medidas disciplinares foram: desligamentos do quadro discente da Instituição, advertências e suspensões, de acordo com a gravidade de cada conduta apurada.

A UniCesumar reafirma seu compromisso com a ética, a responsabilidade, o respeito à vida e os valores que orientam a formação de seus estudantes. A Instituição repudia veementemente qualquer forma de discriminação ou preconceito."

O Conselho Regional de Medicina do Paraná (CRM-PR) informou que as atitudes descritas ferem os princípios do Código de Ética do Estudante de Medicina. Confira:

"Tais atitudes ferem diretamente os princípios fundamentais do Código de Ética do Estudante de Medicina, segundo os quais o estudante deve estar a serviço da saúde do ser humano e da coletividade, exercendo suas atividades sem discriminação de qualquer natureza.

A escolha pela Medicina exige compromissos humanísticos e humanitários, pautados pela promoção do bem-estar físico, mental e social dos indivíduos e da coletividade. Atitudes discriminatórias são incompatíveis com esses valores e não devem ser toleradas no ambiente de formação médica.

O CRM-PR adotará todas as providências cabíveis no âmbito de suas atribuições institucionais e acompanhará o desdobramento do caso, contribuindo para que haja uma apuração rigorosa e transparente dos fatos pelas instâncias competentes".

articles.title: Doula da morte: terapeuta de SP humaniza o fim da vida e o luto | G1
articles.standfirst: Silvia Onofre, de Piracicaba (SP), se dedica à prática ainda pouco difundida no Brasil, que busca humanizar processos com apoio emocional e espiritual a pacientes terminais e famílias.
articles.summary: A doula da morte Silvia Onofre oferece suporte emocional a pacientes terminais e promove retiros de finitude para ressignificar perdas e lutos em Piracicaba.
articles.body:
De clichês populares a reflexões centrais da filosofia, a morte costuma ser encarada como a única certeza da vida, desde a antiguidade com Platão até a era contemporânea de pensadores como Heidegger e Bauman . Enquanto falar de finitude ou se preparar para o fim da vida ainda é tabu mesmo por quem enfrenta o luto, uma prática começa a ganhar espaço: a doulagem da morte .

Em Piracicaba (SP), a professora de ioga e terapeuta integral, Silvia Onofre, decidiu se capacitar para a função de doula da morte e de fim da vida após perder o pai, vítima de câncer, e o cunhado de 36 anos, por um Acidente Vascular Cerebral (AVC), num intervalo de cinco meses em 2017.

Atualmente, ela realiza retiros de finitude como caminho para o bem-viver, grupos voluntários de apoio ao luto, e funeral simbólico.

Silvia Onofre atua como doula da morte em Piracicaba, no interior de São Paulo — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo pessoal

Mas, o que faz uma doula da morte? Ela acompanha pessoas e famílias diante da finitude, do processo de morrer e do luto, oferecendo presença, escuta, apoio emocional e cuidado.

Um ponto importante é que o trabalho das doulas da morte não substitui, em nenhuma medida, o atendimento clínico de médicos, enfermeiros e demais profissionais especializados em cuidados paliativos. É complementar a ele.

No Brasil existem alguns cursos livres para a formação em doulas da morte . Eles abordam, entre outros temas, mitos sobre a finitude, escuta e diretivas antecipadas de vontade e luto.

Silvia Onofre é doula da morte em Piracicaba — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Silvia Onofre

A doulagem da morte (ou doulagem de fim de vida) ainda não é regulamentada no Brasil, diferente da função tradicional de doula, voltada à gestação e ao parto, prevista na Lei Federal nº 15.381/2026.

Após vivenciar duas perdas na família, Silvia Onofre passou a estruturar a carreira com foco no acolhimento e na reflexão sobre o fim da vida.

“A morte faz parte da vida. E falar sobre ela não precisa ser um assunto sombrio” , afirma Silvia em uma de suas postagens nas redes sociais em que apresenta a prática de doula da morte.

Antes de se tornar uma doula da morte, Silvia atuou por mais de dez anos no setor corporativo, em administração escolar.

"Fiz transição de carreira desde a morte do meu pai e do meu cunhado em 2017. Encontrei as doulas da morte na época, mas não estava em momento propício para iniciar a preparação na época. Em 2025, fiz a formação. Desde então, meu trabalho é voltado para a finitude, com educação para a vida e para a morte", relata.

Além da preparação individual, o trabalho inclui atividades em grupo voltadas para a reflexão sobre o tema.

"Ofereço vivências da finitude como um caminho para o bem viver, em que direciono o olhar a nossa finitude para ver como estamos vivendo hoje. A primeira edição do 'Retiro Finitude' foi em março deste ano. Abordei mortes simbólicas, como o término de um relacionamento, uma mudança de emprego ou uma aposentadoria, por exemplo. O segundo retiro será em abril de 2027, com o tema 'Viver é uma Escolha', focado na morte física", explica.

Silvia detalha como funciona a doulagem da morte diante da finitude física.

"A doula da morte é aquela que facilita o espaço para o morrer. Assim, como temos a doula de nascimento, que prepara todo o espaço para o ser vir ao mundo, a doula da morte facilita essa despedida do corpo físico. Ao descobrir uma doença e que vai entrar numa terminalidade, a pessoa pode fazer o preparo para a morte", afirma.

O planejamento do paciente pode envolver questões práticas, desde a organização do velório até documentos formais e legados pessoais.

Jazigo com homenagens durante o Dia de Finados, em Piracicaba — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/ EPTV

A assistência também é voltada para a rede de apoio e familiares envolvidos no processo de perda.

"A pessoa pode escolher o caixão em que quer ser enterrada, a maquiagem, a pintura na unha e deixar diretrizes antecipadas de vontade preparadas. A doula não faz essa mediação com a família", descreveu.

"Ao descobrir que tem uma doença ameaçadora de vida, com pouco tempo, a pessoa também pode escolher por um tratamento tradicional ou cuidado paliativo com acompanhamento médico profissional, que vai tratar o ser humano de forma integral, visando o conforto e não somente o prolongamento da vida. A doula, junto com a equipe médica, pode ajudar na mediação entre os profissionais da saúde, a família e doente", detalhou.

A terapeuta pontua que também é possível trabalhar legados, como escrever cartas ao ente querido e deixá-las com a doula para entrega no pós-morte. A pessoa também pode escolher uma cerimônia no funeral ou alguma música que toque durante o velório, exemplificou.

"Trabalho o atendimento do luto, tanto o luto antecipatório quanto o acolhimento do luto no pós-morte para a família, e também faço o atendimento dos lutos das mortes simbólicas. Esse atendimento de luto é feito por sessões. Além da escuta ativa, trabalho toques, massagens, aromaterapia e algumas posturas de ioga", diz.

Entre os casos atendidos, a terapeuta destaca o uso de rituais para elaborar sentimentos pendentes. "Trabalho também com rituais”, especificou.

Silvia realiza atendimentos particulares, retiros, e também coordena voluntariamente um grupo de apoio ao luto, com cerca de 20 membros, que se encontram mensalmente.

Dezenas de pessoas frequentam as vivências em grupo sobre finitude. “Já participaram média de 35 pessoas”, contou.

A professora Rafaela Pereira Santos, de 38 anos, foi uma das pessoas atendidas pela doula da morte em Piracicaba (SP).

Silvia fez o acolhimento de luto após a demissão inesperada de Rafaela da escola em que trabalhava.

Para Rafaela, que já frequentava as aulas de ioga ministradas por Silvia, a participação no retiro sobre finitude em março de 2026, e o suporte posterior, a ajudaram a ressignificar o encerramento do ciclo profissional e a reorganizar planos pessoais.

"Foram três dias de encontro pessoal e reconexão comigo mesma, um despertar para a vida e para o que eu precisava fazer por mim. Logo em abril, passei por uma dispensa no trabalho e fiquei muito chateada, porque não esperava. A experiência no retiro fortaleceu o olhar meu olhar sobre mim, de ver o que precisava e me deu um norte para seguir uma nova fase", conta Rafaela.

A aliança terapêutica evoluiu para o tratamento de uma ferida antiga: a morte do primeiro filho, Lourenço, ocorrida 11 anos antes em decorrência de complicações provocadas por um pico de pressão arterial no final da gestação.

Com a mãe impossibilitada de acompanhar o velório e o sepultamento devido ao período de internação hospitalar, a doula propôs a realização de uma cerimônia de despedida simbólica para elaborar a dor reprimida.

"Na minha primeira gravidez, tive complicações no final, com 32 semanas. Tive eclâmpsia e acabei perdendo meu bebê. Não pude velar o corpinho do Lourenço, não pude enterrar. A Silvia me sugeriu fazer um velório simbólico. Foi a melhor coisa que poderia ter acontecido, porque, apesar de ter passado todos esses anos, sempre fica uma feridinha aberta. Ficou um momento que eu precisava ter, porque na época eu não pude; fiquei internada por três dias no hospital", relembra.

A experiência permitiu vivenciar o luto de forma adaptada e compreender a abrangência da doulagem, que atua tanto nos momentos de terminalidade física quanto nos processos de encerramento de ciclos e perdas emocionais acumuladas ao longo dos anos.

"Esse trabalho que a Silvia faz é como se você se quisesse dar a oportunidade de viver o luto, mas de uma maneira diferente, com um olhar diferente. A princípio, a gente fica meio receosa em ouvir 'doula da morte'. Mas, depois você compreende que não é só a morte física, mas a morte simbólica, o luto vivenciado de uma separação ou o luto de ter vivido uma saída de um trabalho", comparou.

Com a experiência vivida e a partilha do ensinamento de Silvia, a professora também ressignificou o modo como enxerga a dor do outro.

"Hoje, também consigo olhar para outras pessoas que precisam desse acompanhamento", conclui.

Kelvin Jones, de 26 anos, perdeu a mãe, Íris, vítima de um câncer raro em Piracicaba (SP) — Foto: Kelvin Jones/Arquivo pessoal

O barbeiro Kelvin Jones, de 26 anos, buscou o acolhimento dois meses após a morte da mãe, Íris, vítima de um câncer raro na cabeça. Vivenciando a dor da perda recente, ele encontrou no atendimento o suporte necessário para enfrentar a ausência.

"Conheci a Silvia através de um amigo. Fazia dois meses que eu tinha perdido minha mãe de câncer. Eu estava muito perdido, que sempre era eu e minha mãe, entendeu? Tudo na vida", desabafa Kelvin.

Além da escuta, o processo utiliza técnicas corporais para aliviar as dores físicas causadas pelo luto e orientações para lidar com os pertences deixados.

"A gente às vezes tem muita dor no corpo, o luto traz isso também. Até faz um tipo de uma massagem específica para liberar toda aquela retração. É bem interessante tudo o conhecimento que ela passa e isso alivia a nossa alma", afirma.

O acompanhamento tem auxiliado o jovem a reorganizar a rotina e a processar o impacto da separação de forma mais leve.

"Ela ensina a gente a, de alguma forma, a conseguir fazer ser mais fácil. Não está sendo fácil. Mas, está me ajudando. Foi recente. Há altos e baixos, mas me ajudou muito", finaliza.s

Kelvin, ainda criança, ao lado da mãe, Íris, em foto antiga que morador de Piracicaba (SP) guarda de lembrança — Foto: Kelvin Jones/Arquivo pessoal

Visão médica: dignidade e legado no fim da vida

O suporte profissional no processo de finitude é visto pela medicina como um complemento aos cuidados com a saúde mental. O psiquiatra Arthur Cardoso destaca que a ausência de diálogo sobre o tema torna o luto mais doloroso.

"Ainda existe muito tabu na nossa cultura sobre a morte. No caso de doenças terminais, esse processo de luto pode passar de forma desconfortável, com foco na doença, e não precisa ser dessa forma", avalia o médico.

Para o especialista, o acompanhamento adequado ajuda a preservar a história do paciente e evita complicações emocionais nos familiares.

"Ter um profissional para auxiliar a pessoa a morrer com dignidade, respeitando o legado dela, vem somar aos cuidados. Quando esse processo tem problemas, pode levar a desdobramentos para a família, desde sentimentos de culpa até a sensação de que não houve dignidade", explica Cardoso.

Idoso com cão deitado em sua cama: cuidados paliativos compreendem tudo o que pode ser oferecido a quem tenha uma doença fora de possibilidade de cura — Foto: By Jiří Dušek - Own work, CC BY-SA 4.0

O médico de Família e Comunidade, Lucas Fernando Zorzetto, com trajetória em Unidades Básicas do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) no interior de São Paulo, ressalta a eficiência do trabalho do corpo clínico profissional dedicado aos cuidados paliativos e pondera, em certa medida, a necessidade da prática de doulagem diante da atuação sólida de psicólogos e demais voluntários.

"As equipes de cuidados paliativos são multiprofissionais e interdisciplinares, sendo compostas por médicos, enfermeiros, psicólogos, assistentes sociais, fisioterapeutas, nutricionistas, fonoaudiólogos que atuam em conjunto, além de voluntários como religiosos que oferecem suporte espiritual, avalia o especialista ao citar o Manual de Cuidados Paliativos da Academia Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos (ANCP) e nas diretrizes da Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS).

"O objetivo central desse grupo é garantir o alívio da dor e de sintomas físicos, além de oferecer suporte emocional, social e espiritual integral tanto para o paciente com doença grave quanto para a sua família", completou.

articles.title: 'SNL' co-host Michael Che turns Israel voter turnout into 'genocide' punchline on 'Weekend Update'
articles.summary: Michael Che's Israel "genocide" punchline on "Saturday Night Live" drew sharp rubukes from criticis, including from Campaign Against Antisemitism and NewsBusters.
articles.body: On NBC's "Saturday Night Live," "Weekend Update" co-host Michael Che joked about genocide while discussing voter turnout in Israel's elections, referencing voters on the right and left of the country's political spectrum. "This week, a record number of people voted in Israel’s election, which is great to see regardless of if you’re on the right side, or the left side, or the genocide," Che said. A spokesperson for the Campaign Against Antisemitism acknowledged that the comment was a joke but challenged its premise. "There's always a lot of latitude with comedy, and this joke is hardly an exception," the spokesperson told Fox News Digital. The problem is that it's playing on what has become a widespread but baseless belief that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza." NETANYAHU ALLEGES FRAUD AS ARAB PARTIES SCORE RECORD GAINS — EMERGE AS POTENTIAL KINGMAKERS The organization argued that allegations of genocide against Israel portray Jews as perpetrators of the same crime committed against them during the Holocaust and are "motivated in no small part by a desperation to assuage global guilt for a real genocide against the Jews by casting the Jews as perpetrators of this grave crime themselves." "It has fueled abuse and violence against Jews worldwide — including terrorism and murder," the spokesperson added. NewsBusters managing editor Curtis Houck also criticized the joke, questioning whether viewers understood the meaning of genocide and criticizing the use of the term in discussions about Israel. "We're now at the point where it's a punchline to refer to Israel as a genocidal state," Houck told Fox News Digital. "SNL's ill-informed viewers are unlikely to know the actual meaning of the word, and that it's more applicable to how many Arabs view whether Israel should be allowed to exist." ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE ESCALATES AS DEADLY WEAPON ATTACKS SURGE IN 2025: REPORT Houck argued that the segment could instead have highlighted Arab participation in Israel's election to challenge accusations of genocide. "One could have framed it as a dig against the calls of genocide that a country held free and fair elections in which Arabs could vote and did, to the point their parties won 19 seats in the Knesset, but that would have been too large of a bubble to burst for the far-left in America," Houck said. "Simply put, use of the word ‘genocide’ shouldn't be something to joke about." In Israel's recent election, the nation's two Arab-led parties were projected to secure a combined 19 seats, according to preliminary results. Che delivered the remark alongside co-host Colin Jost during a segment that also targeted President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Republican messaging ahead of Tuesday’s midterm elections. Che previously drew criticism in February 2021 for suggesting that Israel’s COVID-19 vaccination campaign favored Jewish citizens. 'SNL' HOST MICHAEL CHE MOCKS MACKLEMORE'S 'FREE PALESTINE TOUR' AFTER ED SHEERAN DROPS RAPPER "Israel is reporting that they’ve vaccinated half of their population. I’m going to guess it’s the Jewish half," Che said. The Anti-Defamation League (ADL) said the joke "not only missed the mark, but crossed the line." The American Jewish Committee separately sought a retraction and apology from NBC over that segment, saying Che’s suggestion that Israel prioritized Jewish citizens misrepresented vaccine eligibility. The organization said vaccines were available to Israeli citizens regardless of religion or ethnicity. articles.title: Iranian ‘ghost fleet’ filmed evading US blockade en route to China, UANI says
articles.summary: Smaller Iranian ghost fleet tankers are slipping past the U.S. naval blockade carrying sanctioned LPG fuel to China via a shadowy Malaysia anchorage.
articles.body: Small Iranian "ghost fleet" tankers are slipping past the U.S. naval blockade and smuggling sanctioned liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) to China through a shadowy maritime hub off Malaysia, according to U.S. investigators who covertly filmed one of the vessels en route in September. United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI), which conducted the months-long probe, said at least nine similar tankers carrying Iranian oil or LPG have also evaded U.S. restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz since Washington reinstated the Iranian port blockade in July. UANI identified one of the sanctioned tankers as the SOGL. It allegedly escaped the blockade on Sept. 1 carrying approximately 500,000 barrels of Iranian LPG after collecting it at an Iranian port in August. The vessel then traveled thousands of miles to a Malaysian offshore anchorage, where UANI filmed the vessel receiving fuel and other services offshore. The ship then traveled on to China, where the organization said it discharged its Iranian cargo. IRAN’S $800M OIL SMUGGLING SCHEME USES TANKERS POSING AS IRAQI SHIPS TO DODGE BLOCKADE "This tanker had loaded its Iranian LPG from Assaluyeh Port, Iran, in late August. It then breached the U.S. blockade and made its way to a Malaysian anchorage," Jemima Shelley, a senior analyst at UANI, explained. "What this shows us is that some vessels are managing to breach the U.S. maritime blockade," Shelley said of the footage shared exclusively with Fox News Digital. "Most vessels aren't, but since the reinstatement in mid-July, we have seen only nine small tankers being successful in their breach of the U.S. blockade and departing the Gulf of Oman laden with oil or LPG." At the center of the operation is the Malaysian Eastern Outer Port Limits Anchorage, known as the EOPL, an offshore shipping area approximately 70 kilometers from Malaysia’s coastline. The anchorage has become a critical staging ground for Iran’s sanctioned energy trade with China, Shelley said. The area allows vessels to wait offshore, receive supplies and transfer cargo between tankers, providing a logistical lifeline for Iranian energy exports as American naval forces patrol waters closer to Iran. UANI had been monitoring the SOGL before its arrival in Malaysian waters, Shelley explained. US TARGETS CHINESE REFINERY IN SWEEPING IRAN OIL CRACKDOWN, SANCTIONS ‘SHADOW FLEET’ TANKERS "On September 16th, United Against Nuclear Iran chartered a supply vessel and transited 100 nautical miles into the Malaysian Eastern Outer Port Limits Anchorage," Shelley said. "Here we witnessed firsthand the illicit activities of ghost fleet tankers, as well as some Iran-flagged cargo ships that were located in this anchorage, one of them being the SOGL." She described the SOGL as "a Handymax small tanker that was laden with 500,000 barrels of Iranian LPG." The U.S. maritime blockade was first imposed April 13, temporarily lifted in mid-June and reinstated July 14 after diplomatic negotiations collapsed. The operation has largely stopped Iran from exporting crude oil, depriving Tehran of a major source of revenue as the country faces intense economic pressure. "The U.S. blockade is an overwhelming success at preventing vessels laden with Iranian oil and petrochemicals from leaving the Gulf of Oman," Shelley said. She added that since the blockade was reinstated, "no Iranian crude oil has managed to depart and be a successful export for Iran, which is a huge economic pressure for the Iranian regime." "It's just that there are some opportunistic small tankers that are just managing to breach the blockade." The United States, she said, is primarily prioritizing Iranian crude and very large tankers, which often carry "two million barrels of Iranian crude." MORNING GLORY: PRESIDENT TRUMP AND THE AMERICAN MILITARY HAVE BEATEN IRAN LPG is a flammable mixture of hydrocarbons, primarily propane and butane, used for heating, cooking, transportation and industrial production. "LPG carries a lot of risks," Shelley said. "The U.S. blockade's first course of action is to try to attempt to turn around these vessels, which is their main technique for enforcing the U.S. blockade." "However, sometimes they do have to use military force and this would be incredibly high risk on far more volatile cargo such as LPG." According to Shelley, the smaller vessels exploit those challenges while using tactics commonly associated with Iran’s ghost fleet. "So what they'll do is they will turn off their AIS. They will often fly a false flag so they're completely stateless vessels," she added. Automatic Identification System, or AIS, transponders broadcast a vessel’s identity, position and movements to other ships and maritime authorities. Switching them off can make a vessel more difficult to track. "Often they will load, and then they will transit the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, and then in the Gulf of Oman, they will conduct a ship-to-ship transfer there," Shelley said, describing it as a "very high-risk ship-to-ship transfer because it's LPG, not crude oil." "And then the other tanker that's receiving the LPG will then transit and attempt to breach the blockade." The overall scale remains relatively small compared with Iran’s historical energy exports. US ECONOMIC CHOKEHOLD ON IRAN REACHES PEAK LEVERAGE AS COLLAPSE RISKS EMERGE The SOGL, identified by IMO number 9208227, was added to the U.S. Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctions list Oct. 8 over its alleged involvement in transporting Iranian petroleum products since 2025. The vessel has operated under multiple flags, including the Comoros and Zimbabwe, and has been linked in sanctions records to Gravion Maritime Co. "Most of these tankers are very emblematic of what ghost fleet tankers do and so are flying false flags, which means they're completely stateless and will have very complicated front companies running them," Shelley said. Meanwhile, the EOPL anchorage in Malaysia — roughly a 10-day-to-two-week journey from Iran — has become an important logistical center for Iranian vessels traveling toward Chinese buyers and a "key node in Iran's oil trade to China," Shelley said. "It is used by ghost fleet tankers, Iran-flagged tankers that will load Iranian crude and then transit eastwards from Iran all the way to this anchorage where they will often conduct ship-to-ship transfers with the final tanker bound for China." "Often this anchorage is also used for floating storage, which is how Iran managed to survive for so long with the U.S. blockade being reinstated in July," Shelley said. She also clarified that since the blockade has been enforced, Iranian floating storage has fallen to "zero to seven million barrels." "So you can see how they have survived from having this offshore anchorage where illicit ghost fleet tankers have been able to wait laden with Iranian products." IRAN’S OIL LIFELINE IS DRYING UP. THE BIGGEST PAIN MAY FALL ON ORDINARY CITIZENS UANI’s video also shows the SOGL sitting low in the water and receiving bunkering services from a smaller tanker off Malaysia, where Shelley said authorities appear to be "looking the other way." "This is a common thing that you will see in this anchorage, because not only is this anchorage used for ship-to-ship transfers, but also these ghost fleet tankers, as well as some cargo ships in this anchorage, require various services, whether that is food, logistics or bunker fuel." China is the dominant destination for Iranian oil and LPG, providing Tehran with a critical economic outlet despite U.S. sanctions and the naval blockade. "For years, China has made up 80% of Iran's liquid cargo exports, and we have seen that only grow since the beginning of the Iran War. Now China is importing almost 100% of Iran's oil and LPG exports." "It has created a system and trade that has allowed Iran to avoid sanctions, U.S. and OPEC sanctions, whilst China is able to buy highly discounted Iranian oil and LPG." IRAN SEIZES SHIPS IN HORMUZ AS US TALKS FALTER AFTER CEASEFIRE EXTENSION "After United Against Nuclear Iran's trip to the EOPL, interestingly, this small LPG tanker SOGL did not conduct a ship-to-ship transfer," Shelley said. "Instead, it transited northbound into the South China Sea, where it finally discharged its Iranian LPG at Xinzhou Port in China." The G Summer, a U.S.-sanctioned LPG carrier with a capacity of approximately 7,000 cubic meters, was also separately tracked transmitting signals from the Arabian Sea beyond the American blockade line in April, according to Bloomberg. The vessel broadcast a message indicating it had an "all Chinese crew" aboard, while shipping analytics identified Iran as its last cargo country and Galle, Sri Lanka, as its reported destination. articles.title: Nine die in ‘cataclysmic’ Florida business jet crash
articles.summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis tells reporters there appeared to be no casualties on the ground.
articles.body:
Nine people have died after a business jet crashed into a residential neighbourhood in South Florida , the United States.

All on board were killed in the crash, which US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described as a “horrific tragedy” in a post on X on Sunday.

Federal Aviation Administration staff were on their way to the crash site to support a National Transportation Safety Board investigation into the incident, Duffy said.

Disturbing recordings in the plane’s cockpit shortly before the crash, retained by LiveATC.net, captured the pilot talking about “manageable” ice issues, before later saying the plane was rapidly losing altitude.

Shortly after, the panicked crew said, “We’re going to crash into the ground”.

The plane was a Learjet 60 – a popular business jet – heading from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas. Austin-Bergstrom International airport confirmed that the plane was a private jet, but not who was on board.

Videos of the incident circulating online appear to show the jet striking the ground at high speed and on a sharp angle, followed by a huge explosion.

Footage of the aftermath appears to show flames flickering around debris and chunks of pavement, with people milling around the area.

The plane looked to have fallen just metres from homes and cars, but Florida Governor Ron DeSantis told reporters that there appeared to be no casualties on the ground.

Speaking from the scene, DeSantis described the crash as “cataclysmic” and said the plane “looked like a missile going down, and left a big crater on the side of the road”.

articles.title: A&E warning system to flag dangerously ill children
articles.summary: The initiative, in England, will help busy staff identify children who are deteriorating quickly as they wait for emergency care.
articles.body:
A new early warning system is being introduced in hospital emergency departments in England to help busy NHS staff identify sick children who are dangerously deteriorating.

It comes after Health Secretary Yvette Cooper promised to stop "corridor care" for sick children because of long waits for hospital beds.

The new National Paediatric Early Warning System (PEWS) asks staff to check, log and grade vital signs, such as blood pressure, heart rate and oxygen levels.

A high overall score means a child needs more urgent attention. Concerns from staff, parents, carers or the child themselves will trigger an immediate escalation of care.

The initiative is designed to save lives ahead of winter, when pressure on the NHS is at its highest.

On the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Cooper recently talked about the case of two-year-old Finlay Roberts, who died in 2024 after spending hours in a hospital corridor before being discharged.

Cooper apologised to Finlay's parents on behalf of the NHS, saying: "No child should be treated in a corridor. No patient should be treated in a corridor."

Whittington Health NHS Trust, where Finlay waited for treatment, extended its condolences to the family and said it continued to experience periods of exceptional demand across emergency care and, at times, some patients may receive care in temporary clinical areas, including corridors.

A similar "early warning" system to identify acutely ill adults, including those with sepsis, is already in use in emergency and general NHS hospital wards.

More than 90 hospitals across England have been using the alert system in children's wards, with different age-appropriate assessments available for babies through to teenagers.

The NHS has already said it will expand Martha's Rule to all hospital emergency departments in England. The rule gives patients, families and carers the right to request a rapid review if they are worried that a patient's condition is getting worse and their concerns are not being responded to.

The initiative is named after Martha Mills, who died aged 13 in 2021 after developing blood poisoning, or sepsis, in hospital following a bike accident.

A coroner ruled that her family's concerns about her worsening condition were not listened to and she would probably have survived had she been moved to intensive care earlier.

Martha's parents Merope and Paul came up with the idea of the rule in a bid to change the culture that contributed to her death.

A&E units will have a dedicated phone number that can be called to trigger an urgent review of a patient's care.

Duncan Burton, chief nursing officer for England, said the new early warning system for children in emergency departments was an "important next step in improving care for children and young people across England for this winter - and beyond".

He added: "In fast-paced emergency departments, staff need to spot quickly when a child's condition is deteriorating.

"This standardised approach will help them recognise the warning signs, communicate concerns, and make timely decisions when every moment matters."

The early warning system for children, PEWS, is a collaboration between NHS England and the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health and the Royal College of Nursing.

articles.title: Russia, Ukraine air raid alert apps hit by cyberattacks after truce ends
articles.summary: Ukrainian users receive fake warnings of nuclear threats, while Moscow reports ‘false information’ on its app.
articles.body:
Russia has said its emergency warnings app came under a “massive cyberattack”, hours after Kyiv’s announcement that Ukraine’s air raid alert app was hacked.

Moscow’s Emergencies Ministry said on Telegram early on Monday morning that the cyberattack led to the spread of “false information” on the app, which warns users of incoming drone attacks.

The ministry did not say who was behind the cyberattack.

Earlier on Sunday evening local time, the Ukrainian Air Force said that users received fake alerts warning of nuclear and chemical threats to areas in and around Kyiv, along with warnings of potential street combat.

An erroneous message also said Russia’s hypersonic Oreshnik missile had been deployed.

“The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence,” the Ukrainian Air Force said on Telegram on Sunday. “There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel.”

SPRAVDI, Ukraine’s Centre for Strategic Communications, blamed Russia for the hack in a post on X.

The air raid alert app is used across Ukraine to warn people in real time of incoming Russian air attacks. A separate app, specifically for the Ukrainian capital, was working normally, according to Kyiv authorities.

The announcements from Russia and Ukraine follow the end of a truce between the two countries in a part of the Russian-occupied Kherson region.

The localised ceasefire , which began on Tuesday and ended on Sunday, was the longest of the war so far.

articles.title: Missing Utah teen Kylie Arellano found safe in Oregon after 500-day search
articles.summary: Kylie Arellano was found safe in Oregon with a 39-year-old man after vanishing from Utah more than 500 days ago, ending a massive FBI search.
articles.body: A Utah teenager who vanished nearly a year and a half ago has been found safe in Oregon, ending a lengthy nationwide search that spanned more than 500 days. Kylie Arellano, now 17, was last seen by her family on May 29, 2025, at their home in Garden City, Utah, when she was 15 years old. Kylie's disappearance had triggered a wide federal and state investigation that led officials through dozens of unconfirmed sightings before culminating in her recovery on Sunday. MISSING TEEN FOUND HIDING IN CONVICTED SEX OFFENDER'S CLOSET IN FLORIDA, SHERIFF SAYS Law enforcement officers in Oregon, working directly with the FBI's Salt Lake City field office and the Rich County Sheriff's Office, safely recovered the teen, according to a law enforcement news release. Kylie, they said, was found with a 39-year-old man in Oregon. The man was taken into custody without incident. "The FBI and the Rich County Sheriff’s Office have been actively investigating this case for more than a year and pursuing every lead received from across the U.S. and in other countries. FBI NABS MORE THAN 350 ALLEGED CHILD SEX ABUSE OFFENDERS "As this case is ongoing, no further information will be released at this time," the FBI's Salt Lake City field office said in a statement on Sunday. Federal authorities also credited the Oregon State Police, the FBI's Portland field office and the Utah Department of Public Safety for their assistance in the operation. "Tonight, local police in Oregon brought a minor who had been missing for a year and a half to safety, acting on information provided by our FBI Salt Lake City Field Office," FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital. "We are grateful she can return home, and we will continue working with our partners to hold those responsible accountable," Patel added. MIKE WALTZ, TIM TEBOW LAUNCH EFFORT TO COMBAT ONLINE CHILD EXPLOITATION: 'IT'S HAPPENING IN THEIR BACKYARD' "To anyone using gore groups to target and exploit children: the FBI and our partners are coming for you. "We are using every tool at our disposal to combat nihilistic violent extremism, bring offenders to justice and protect America’s children." Kylie Arellano’s grandmother also thanked the authorities for finding her. "THANK YOU for all you and your agents and teams are doing to find our baby girl, Kylie Arellano and bring her home!!!" she wrote on X. According to a law enforcement source, the suspect allegedly met the teenager on Snapchat before her disappearance. Last year, Rich County Sheriff Dale Stacey said detectives had chased reports of sightings across multiple states and urged the public to preserve any photographic or timestamped evidence. TWO MISSING CHILDREN RESCUED FROM TRAILER AS POLICE ARREST BABYSITTER ON KIDNAPPING CHARGES New details about the investigation had also emerged days before Kylie was found. Unsealed search warrants reviewed by KUTV on Oct. 29 showed that investigators had previously scrutinized Kylie's mother, Stephanie Coleman, and questioned her about a 2024 allegation of physical abuse. There were also questions about discrepancies involving missing text messages from the night Kylie vanished and suspicious marks in the home. Coleman had denied having any role in her daughter's disappearance or abusing her, providing timestamped "good night" text messages from May 29, 2025. articles.title: J&K: NC Srinagar MP Mehdi to quit party tomorrow to fight it back on 'ideological' turf
articles.summary: BUDGAM: At the entrance of the National Conference (NC) Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi home’s two large banners at the gate sum up the message he wants to
articles.body: BUDGAM: At the entrance of the National Conference (NC) Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi home’s two large banners at the gate sum up the message he wants to convey. One reads, “Wada kursi se bada hai” (a promise is bigger than a chair), while the other says, “Kirdar ki siyasat, usoolon ki siyasat” (politics of character, politics of principles).Inside the hall, party workers gathered in small groups, discussing the fallout of Mehdi's announcement that he would formally resign from as NC MP at a rally here on November 3 on the death anniversary of his father. One worker said, “even at a barber's shop, people do not give up their chairs for someone else even if that person is older. Here is a man willing to leave his chair for the sake of principles. Who gives up a chair like that.”Inside in his room, sitting calmly in his chair, Mehdi insists his decision to part ways with the party is final and there is no going back.“I have been part of this NC for 24 years. I joined it believing that it stood for autonomy and the rights of the people of J&K. But after the abrogation of Article 370, whatever remnants of autonomy we had were taken away and the party despite getting a strong mandate in the 2024 Assembly elections on the promise of challenging the status quo, failed to honour it,” Mehdi told the TOI, accusing the chief minister Omar Abdullah of diluting his electoral position on Article 370, Waqf Amendment Act, Muslim issues, reservations and moving closer to the BJP, “to the point of submission.”In the room, hanging on the wall was a large photograph of his father, Aga Syed Mehdi, a prominent Shia cleric and Congress leader who was assassinated in a terrorist attack on November 3, 2000.“I understand it will be long fight but I am not afraid," he said, hastily added that whenever the NC faced an ideological challenge, it found it tough to defend its position. The People’s Democratic Party (PDP) managed, he said, for a brief period, to offer it such a challenge before joining an alliance with the BJP in 2015 reduced party to three members today. “There was also an ideological contest between the NC and the Hurriyat Conference in Jammu and Kashmir for many years. I am not endorsing the Hurriyat Conference as it represented the other extreme. But when it came to ideological contestation, the streets were dominated by the other side, not the National Conference,” he said.He said people need to replace traditional political forces like NC and PDP and other like them with more potent one having conviction. “The common problem with these two political parties and others like them, is their lack of character. It is what they have in common. People trusted the NC and the PDP. But they delivered the same kind of results,” he added.Mehdi, who has been critical of the CM and his government, said the chief minister normalised the post-abrogation arrangement through his government, Assembly and other constitutional institutions. “The party began speaking the very language that the BJP wanted people across the country to speak after the abrogation of Article 370,” he said. He said he found further clarity after NC president Farooq Abdullah recently said in an interview that if Mehdi believed what he says he was free to resign from the party.“Referring to me Dr Abdullah said that if I believed Article 370 could be restored, I was free to move out and get it restored. Effectively, he was saying that he himself did not believe Article 370 could not be restored. This again raises the question, if he does not believe it can be restored constitutionally, why people of Jammu and Kashmir were given the assurance during the poll campaign. In the same interview, he asked me to resign from the party as, in his view, I had become an irritant in the process of normalising the post-abrogation status quo. They wanted me to leave the party because I am questioning their position,” he added.Mehdi also rejected the claim that the NC alone was responsible for his victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Srinagar. “The NC never crossed 1.5 lakh votes in this parliamentary constituency in 30 to 40 years. This time I got nearly 3.80 lakh votes. The bulk of the support came from people in South Kashmir who were not associated with the NC,” he said as number of areas of South Kashmir’s Pulwama and Shopian were added to Srinagar in the delimitation exercise of 2023. He, however, said that he contested on the NC ticket and used the party's name and symbol, making his resignation necessary as he sought to distance himself from the organisation.Mehdi, who is also a prominent shia leader, said he was reaching out to people from different walks of life, including journalists, lawyers, doctors and teachers, to build a credible political alternative.“I am looking for people with no baggage, who have conviction and are willing to walk this path,” he said, adding that the structure and name of any new organisation would be decided later.He said he might contest future by-elections from Srinagar constituency as an independent candidate but insisted his decision to resign was not driven by electoral ambition. “I am not bargaining with people over what I will get in return for resigning. This has nothing to do with electoral results or how people behave. It is a call of conscience and a matter of principles,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Juan Atkins, co-creator of the techno music genre, has died
articles.summary: Influenced by author Alvin Toffler and radio DJ The Electrifying Mojo, Atkins and friends created techno in 1980s Detroit.
articles.body: Juan Atkins, who helped create the techno music genre with school friends in suburban Detroit in the 1980s, has died, his booking agency said Sunday. He was 64. Collaborator Kevin Saunderson also shared the news on his Facebook page, saying, “Juan was the originator of Techno, a true visionary who opened the door for so many of us, myself included.” Atkins, who played techno records as a noted club and festival DJ, was scheduled to perform Saturday at the club Yu Yu in Mexico City, but the appearance was canceled, the club said on Instagram before news of his death broke. In 1981, Atkins formed a duo, Cybotron, with Richard Davis, a friend he met at a Detroit-area community college, and in 1983 they released “Clear,” a robotic, futuristic dance track that resonated in clubland and in breakdancers’ boomboxes, according to the duo’s Discogs biography. The foundations of techno — Kraftwerk, Afrika Bambaataa, breakdancing hip-hop known as electro and the post-disco sound of house music — were present as Atkins and friends from Belleville High School, about 35 miles west of downtown Detroit, tinkered with electronic music and listened to the weird, wild sounds of radio DJ The Electrifying Mojo. Atkins, Saunderson and Derrick May were nicknamed the Belleville Three. May told the Detroit Metro Times last year that the trio, along with Atkins’ brother, Aaron, would skip school and listen to jazz. “I was so impressed and enamored with Juan and Aaron that I just followed them, man — I just became Juan’s disciple,” May told the Metro Times. Saunderson had the biggest early success when his act, Inner City, released “Big Fun” and “Good Life,” which became club hits in the U.S. and the U.K. in 1988. Atkins became the genre’s wiseman. Techno’s origin story as a rebel sound rooted in visions of a dystopian, digital future was born of Atkins’ fascination with author Alvin Toffler’s “The Third Wave,” according to author Dan Sicko’s “Techno Rebels.” Cybotron’s 1984 release, “Techno City,” is a bittersweet ode to a Detroit that was collapsing in places as the U.S. economy recovered from recession. Inner City’s subsequent success helped make the Belleville Three stars in Europe, just as the Berlin Wall fell. Berlin would take over as techno’s capital. The Belleville Three found fans and gigs in Europe but bemoaned dance music fans who believe techno was created there. (“Techno is Black,” the Metro Times declared last year.) Missy Elliott put Detroit techno on pop music’s map by sampling Cybotron’s “Clear” for 2005’s “Lose Control.” And in 2023, Atkins revived Cybotron with the help of Berlin producer Laurens von Oswald by releasing new music on the Tresor label. Techno’s Detroit roots found reinforcement from the city’s Movement Festival (“Experience the birthplace of Techno,” it said), and the NBA’s Pistons’ release of clothing that pays homage to the Belleville Three. “Detroit is home,” the trio said in a joint statement about the clothing release in January. “Everything we’ve ever made started with this city, its people, its clubs, and its energy.” In the trio’s wake came techno’s telltale, “boom-tss” sound, as performed by Jeff Mills, Richie Hawtin, the Underground Resistance crew, DJ Hell and Carl Cox. “It’s with a heavy heart to hear about the passing of Juan Atkins,” Cox said Sunday on Facebook, adding that Cybotron’s “Clear” “never left my soul.” German techno star Sven Väth called the news of Atkins’ death “heartbreaking.” “His vision inspired generations and helped build a musical bridge between Detroit and Berlin,” he said on Instagram. “Juan was truly ahead of his time.” Väth concluded, “Your music, your vision and your spirit will live on.”

articles.title: US midterms: What to know about independent voters and candidates
articles.summary: Despite a record number of independents, third-party candidates and voters struggle to penetrate the two-party system.
articles.body:
As Americans head to the polls on Tuesday in the much-anticipated midterms , the record number of voters identifying as independent could prove decisive for control of the US Congress and state legislatures .

Nearly half of US voters – as many as 117 million adults – now identify as politically independent, with the two major parties, Democrats and Republicans, jockeying for their votes.

At the same time, independent or third-party candidates win few federal or state seats. The Democratic and Republican parties have dominated US politics, from state legislatures to the US Congress and the presidency, for generations.

“The whole [electoral] system is built to frustrate the independence of voters,” says Rick Bennett, the former Republican Party chair in Maine, where he is running to become only the third independent governor in the state’s history.

Bennett’s candidacy runs headlong into one of the most stubborn contradictions in US politics: While millions of eligible voters reject Republican and Democratic labels , far fewer will cast their ballots for independent candidates.

“For decades, candidates outside the Democratic and Republican parties have struggled to achieve [a high] level of support,” political scientist AJ Simmons said. “[But] 2026 is shaping up to be one of the strongest election cycles for independent candidates in recent memory.”

Who are independents and how will they vote?

According to the Pew Research Center’s annual National Public Opinion Reference Survey, 44 percent of US adults identify as politically independent. This is in contrast to 29 percent who identify as Democrat and 28 percent as Republican.

But there is a caveat: Most self-described independents still gravitate towards one of the major parties. Independents who express absolutely no partisan leaning make up only about 7-10 percent of the total electorate.

These “true” independents are sought after by candidates because they are persuadable, the core of the coveted so-called swing vote in a deeply divided and partisan electorate and political system.

In the 2026 midterm elections, 52 percent of likely independent voters are supporting Democrats, while 39 percent back Republicans, polling firm Marist suggests.

Frustration with President Donald Trump is permeating the midterm electoral landscape, with independent respondents more than three times as likely to say their vote is mainly against the president, and 28 percent saying they are voting for “change”.

Why does the US have a two-party system?

The US does not legally restrict elections to two parties, and many local officials are not party-affiliated.

But for more powerful federal and statewide seats like Tuesday’s House of Representatives and Senate races, the winner-take-all electoral system and single-member congressional districts work against outsiders and can discourage voters from backing them.

Even substantial support for a minor party is rarely concentrated enough in one district to win a congressional seat.

Voters, too, can unknowingly reinforce the system.

Polling trends and data further suggest that voters who identify as or prefer an independent will often instead back a Republican or Democrat they see as more politically viable. Voters are also reluctant to support “spoilers”, who may peel away votes from one of the two major-party candidates.

Why do third parties struggle to win US elections?

Bernard Tamas, a political scientist at Valdosta State University who studies third parties, said that although laws are often blamed for keeping third-party candidates off the ballot, “there is very little evidence that legal barriers are undermining these candidates”.

A total of $14.8bn was spent on federal elections during the 2024 presidential cycle, and the 2026 midterms are projected to surpass that, reaching up to $11.6bn in political advertisement spending alone.

The Democratic National Committee (DNC), which heads the Democratic Party, raised nearly $252.3m during the 2026 midterm campaign cycle while the Republican National Committee (RNC) took in about $341m.

Unlike other democracies, the US “offers virtually no public support” or funding to political parties and does not set limits on campaign spending”, Tamas said. Independent candidates “raise very little money” and are less well known by voters.

Why don’t more Americans vote independent?

Lesley Shedd, a Republican strategist, told Al Jazeera that the surge in voters identifying as independents obscures their support for one of the two major parties.

“When somebody says they are independent, they really are a Republican or Democrat but they maybe don’t agree with the party on absolutely every issue,” Shedd said. “Or they [just] don’t want to feel as though they are part of the culture of the swamp of [Washington] DC.”

The real test for independent candidates is persuading Americans to vote for them, not just a “protest vote” against the system. And voters are reluctant to cast a “wasted” ballot, Simmons said, given the most competitive candidates are Democrats or Republicans.

There are efforts to support independent candidates. The Independent Leadership Council, launched in July by former Democrat-turned-independent Senator Joe Manchin, provides donors and campaign resources for independent congressional candidates. The project has raised more than $10m.

But the longer-term test, analysts maintain, is whether independent candidates can be viable across multiple races and election cycles.

Will third-party candidates influence the 2026 midterms?

There is currently one independent in the US House and two in the US Senate. None holds a state governor seat.

Bennett, the independent Maine candidate, is one of just 11 independent or third-party candidates vying for gubernatorial or US Senate seats whom Simmons expects to surpass the 5 percent vote threshold often used to gauge electoral viability.

Additionally, Simmons sees several ways independent congressional hopefuls could throw the midterm map into disarray, mainly in two key states: Nebraska and Montana.

He identified Nebraska’s independent Senate candidate Dan Osborn, a 51-year-old Navy veteran, as the “most likely alternative candidate to win” across the country, given the race has been deemed a toss-up by RealClearPolling, an election analysis website.

The Nebraska Democratic Party chose not to field a replacement nominee after its candidate withdrew, leaving Osborn as the principal challenger to Republican Pete Ricketts.

In Montana, Simmons sees another opening for an independent, though the race is complicated by the possibility of an unpredictable “spoiler” effect.

Seth Bodnar, a former University of Montana president and Army veteran, is running against Republican Kurt Alme for the US Senate seat. He is being backed by the Independent Leadership Council, which is also supporting California Congressman Kevin Kiley, who left the Republican Party to seek re-election as an independent.

Democratic US Senate candidate Alani Bankhead could siphon off support from the same centre-left and anti-Republican pool of voters that Bodnar draws from, risking a three-way vote and potentially leaving the Republican to collect the spoils.

“Montana is the second most likely,” Simmons said, adding that “if that were to happen, the Republican Party would be having an extraordinarily bad night”.

In Idaho and South Dakota, independent candidates are not forecast to win, but they are expected to make Republicans pay for treating those seats as safe, diverting money, campaign time and attention to races Republicans may have otherwise taken for granted.

The greatest impact of independents may be the pressure they have historically brought to bear on the major parties to “implement a new policy or govern more effectively”, Simmons said.

articles.title: Write-In Ralph: South Carolina Republicans challenge Trump’s Senate pick
articles.summary: As Trump supports Senator Darline Graham, one conservative group is rallying around someone else.
articles.body:
Charleston, South Carolina – Avery Milton thought he was a die-hard supporter of US President Donald Trump. The 28-year-old South Carolina native had voted for Trump in the past three elections and believed in his promise to put America first. But ahead of the midterm elections, the president has left him feeling betrayed.

“He stabbed us in the back during his second term,” Milton told Al Jazeera.

Milton’s disillusionment is not isolated. He said many people close to him share this frustration, particularly younger conservatives around his age who are starting families and entering the workforce. Trump launching a war on Iran, after campaigning on a promise to avoid new wars, was a particular breaking point.

Now, Milton is helping lead a grassroots effort to write in Republican Congressman Ralph Norman for the US Senate, rather than support the party nominee, Senator Darline Graham , who has Trump’s endorsement.

A write-in candidate is someone whose name does not appear on the ballot but can still be chosen by voters who write it in themselves. The option is often used to indicate dissatisfaction with the official candidates, but rarely leads to a victory. One of those rare victories happened in 2010, when Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska won after launching a write-in campaign, having lost her Republican primary that year.

In the 2022 South Carolina Senate race, write-in votes accounted for just 0.1 percent of all votes cast.

Despite the president’s endorsement, Graham has struggled to unite conservatives behind her, potentially giving Democratic challenger Annie Andrews an opening in a state that has not elected a Democrat to the US Senate since 1998.

Darline’s unlikely path to Republican Senate candidate

After the sudden death of Republican US Senator Lindsey Graham on July 11, his younger sister, Darline, was appointed to serve out the remainder of his term.

Her appointment followed a tradition of family members succeeding deceased lawmakers, most commonly their spouses. But she made history as the first sibling appointed to fill a Senate vacancy.

Graham initially described the role as an opportunity to finish her brother’s work during the remaining months of his term. But days later, Trump urged her to run for a full six-year term, posting “RUN, DARLINE, RUN!” on Truth Social and promising his “complete and total endorsement” if she entered the race. Three days later, Graham announced on Fox News that she would run.

For some Republicans, the transition from temporary appointment to a full-term campaign happened too quickly. Milton said he felt the appointment had effectively “installed” a candidate.

Graham went on to defeat Republican Ralph Norman in the state’s August primary elections.

Norman, who represents South Carolina’s fifth congressional district, has repeatedly declined to campaign alongside Graham since losing the primary. He has made clear that his support for Graham is limited.

“You have to earn the vote. She hasn’t done that,” he told The Wall Street Journal. “The campaign has been about trying to prop up a candidate.”

The tensions have been particularly pronounced in Upstate South Carolina, where Norman has considerable support. Milton said Graham has done little to reach voters there during the campaign, aside from private dinners and appearances alongside Trump.

“She [Graham] never tried to reach out to everyday people here Upstate. And that spoke volumes about how this South Carolina GOP establishment feels about the grassroots conservatives. They just really don’t care,” Milton said.

Frustrated by what he saw as a failure to represent grassroots conservatives, Milton helped launch the Write-In Ralph movement, building a website and giving the campaign a public platform.

Milton said he and other supporters wanted a senator who would think independently, rather than simply fall in line with party leadership.

“We don’t necessarily want somebody that’s a rubber stamp for everything,” he said, adding that he wanted someone willing to “think of all the sides of an issue and policy”.

A sizeable group of South Carolina voters does not identify with either major party.

While the state does not register voters by party, a New York Times/Siena poll conducted in October suggested that 30 percent of likely voters identified as independents. Among those voters, Democratic Senate candidate Andrews led Graham by 20 percentage points.

The findings point to a potential blind spot for Republicans seeking to consolidate support around Trump’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) coalition.

John Connolly, a 77-year-old retiree who lives in South Carolina’s Lowcountry, is one example of a voter whose political allegiances have shifted over time. He sees Graham’s appointment as part of a political culture that rewards loyalty over experience.

“I see her as nothing more than a puppet,” he told Al Jazeera. “To nod her head yes whenever she’s told to.”

Leila Ali, a regional campaign adviser who has spent more than a decade working with grassroots organisations across the US South, said political strategists often underestimate the diversity of the Southern electorate.

“The biggest thing that people get wrong is that they think the Southern vote is this monolith,” she told Al Jazeera.

Ali pointed to South Carolina’s early voting figures as evidence of that engagement. Nearly 950,000 early votes have been cast in the state, according to the state’s Election Commission, setting a new record for early voting in a midterm election.

The stakes of this race have become increasingly apparent as the November 3 election approaches.

Despite Trump winning South Carolina by nearly 18 percentage points in 2024, he has made two trips to South Carolina in three months to campaign for Graham – an extraordinary show of presidential attention.

And polling suggests the race is far more competitive than Republicans might have expected. The October New York Times/Siena College poll had Graham and Democratic challenger Annie Andrews tied at 48 percent among likely voters.

For Democrats, this division offers a rare opening in a deep-red state where the party has struggled to compete.

Even with the race tightening, Republicans like Milton are willing to risk a Democratic victory by writing in Ralph Norman on their ballot. And if Graham loses, Milton says the blame should not fall on the write-in effort.

“They’re going to try to point the finger on this Write-in Ralph movement,” he said. “But I just want to make something very clear: that would assume that our votes would have gone to Darline anyway, and that’s just not the case.”

articles.body: A South Korean army staff sergeant died after sustaining external injuries at a frontline military unit in Cheorwon, near the border with North Korea, on Monday morning, the country's Defence Ministry said.Military and civilian investigators are examining the cause and circumstances of his death, the ministry said, Reuters reports.It was not immediately clear whether the sergeant's death was connected to the border tensions.The incident comes after three South Korean soldiers were wounded in landmine explosions south of the Military Demarcation Line on September 21. The blasts had added to tensions between the two Koreas, which remain technically at war as they have never signed a peace treaty following the 1950-53 Korean War.South Korea's military has accused North Korea of laying the mines as part of efforts to fortify the border since 2024. Pyongyang has denied the allegation.The latest incident is likely to draw attention to security conditions along the heavily fortified border, where military activity and occasional incidents have kept tensions between the two neighbours high.You use AI every day.
